items.stem: What is consumer surplus?
options: The difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay
The difference between price and cost
items.answer: The difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay
items.markingKey: Area below the demand curve and above the price.

items.stem: Explain the meaning of consumer surplus and how it can be shown on a diagram.
items.answer: Consumer surplus is the extra benefit consumers receive because they pay less than the maximum they are willing to pay. It is the area under the demand curve and above the market price, up to the quantity bought.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition; 1 mark: area on diagram [2]

items.stem: Explain why a rise in the price of a good reduces consumer surplus.
items.answer: Consumers who still buy pay more, losing some surplus, and some consumers stop buying altogether, losing all their surplus.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: existing buyers pay more; 1 mark: some buyers leave [2]

items.stem: The demand for electric scooters is Qd = 88 − 4P and supply is Qs = −20 + 5P, with Q in thousands and P in dollars. The market is in equilibrium. Calculate consumer surplus.

The demand for smartphones is Qd = 110 − 5P and supply is Qs = 10 + 5P, with Q in thousands and P in dollars. The market is in equilibrium. (a) Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity and the consumer surplus. (b) The price rises to $12. Calculate the new consumer surplus and the loss of consumer surplus. (c) Explain the two parts of this loss.
items.answer: (a) P = $10, Q = 60; CS = $360,000. (b) Q = 50; CS = $250,000; loss $110,000. (c) Remaining buyers pay more (rectangle), and buyers priced out lose all their surplus (triangle).
items.markingKey: (a) equilibrium [1]; CS = ½ × (22 − 10) × 60 [1] (b) new CS [1]; loss [1] (c) two parts [1] [5]

items.stem: Extract: The market for chocolate bars in Seoul is described by Qd = 140 − 5P and Qs = −40 + 10P (Q in thousands per month, P in dollars). The city council is considering a tax on chocolate bars, which some councillors say would “simply transfer money from consumers to the council”. (a) Calculate consumer surplus at equilibrium. (b) Calculate producer surplus at equilibrium.
On a demand and supply diagram, consumer surplus is the area
options: above the supply curve and below the price
between the demand and supply curves to the right of equilibrium
below the demand curve and above the market price
items.answer: below the demand curve and above the market price
items.markingKey: Triangle between D and price line.

items.stem: Felix would have paid up to $120 for a concert ticket in Santiago but bought it for $75. Explain what is meant by Felix’s consumer surplus and calculate it.
items.answer: Consumer surplus is the difference between willingness to pay and the price paid: $120 − $75 = $45.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition; 1 mark: $45 [2]

items.stem: An airline in Lunaria charges different fares to different passengers on the same flight. Explain how this reduces consumer surplus.
items.answer: By charging prices closer to each passenger’s willingness to pay, the airline turns consumer surplus into revenue (price discrimination).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: prices nearer willingness to pay; 1 mark: surplus captured by firm [2]

items.answer: Willingness to pay vs price; area under demand above price; price fall raises CS (existing + new buyers); diagram.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Willingness to pay vs price; area under demand above price; price fall raises CS (existing + new buyers); diagram. Level 3 (6–8): accurate knowledge with a clear, developed analytical chain and, where relevant, an accurate, labelled diagram that is used in the answer; Level 2 (3–5): some correct explanation but undeveloped or partly inaccurate; Level 1 (1–2): limited knowledge, mostly assertion [8]

items.stem: What is producer surplus?
options: The difference between the price producers receive and the minimum price at which they are willing to supply
The surplus stock held by producers
items.answer: The difference between the price producers receive and the minimum price at which they are willing to supply
items.markingKey: Area above supply curve and below price.

items.stem: Explain the meaning of producer surplus.
items.answer: The extra amount producers receive above the minimum price at which they would have been willing to supply each unit; the area above the supply curve and below the market price.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition; 1 mark: area [2]

items.stem: Explain why an increase in demand increases producer surplus.
items.answer: Price rises, so existing output earns more above its minimum supply price, and extra output is supplied at the higher price, adding more surplus.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: higher price on existing units; 1 mark: extra units [2]

items.stem: The supply of paper is Qs = −10 + 6P and demand is Qd = 80 − 3P, with Q in thousands and P in dollars. The market is in equilibrium at P = $10. Calculate producer surplus.

The supply of bottled water is Qs = −30 + 10P and demand is Qd = 74 − 3P, with Q in thousands and P in dollars. The market is in equilibrium at P = $8. (a) Calculate the equilibrium quantity and the producer surplus. (b) Calculate consumer surplus. (c) Explain what the total of the two surpluses represents.
items.answer: (a) Q = 50; PS = $125,000. (b) CS = $416,667. (c) Total economic welfare = $541,667: the net benefit to consumers and producers from trade in this market.

items.answer: They receive a higher price for every bag sold above the minimum they would accept, so producer surplus rises (if their own output is unaffected).

items.stem: If supply increases and demand is unchanged, what happens to consumer surplus?
items.answer: It increases

items.stem: Explain how an increase in supply affects consumer surplus and producer surplus.
items.answer: Price falls and quantity rises: consumer surplus rises (lower price, more buyers); producer surplus may rise or fall depending on the elasticity of demand and the shift.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: CS rises; 1 mark: PS effect with reason [2]

items.stem: Explain why an indirect tax creates a deadweight loss.
items.answer: The tax raises price and reduces quantity; trades that would have given benefits greater than costs no longer happen, so some consumer and producer surplus is lost and not collected as tax.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: fewer trades; 1 mark: surplus lost not transferred [2]
